verdicts.evidence: readColdSessionLog from @deepseek-ai/dsh-session-query (0.2.0-rc.2) is an exported standalone function taking a SessionPersistence; it mounted in a bare Cordis Context and read a real 75-event v4 session from the external Palimpsest process with no model call and no agent activation.

5 tests read a real session (37 known events, all seven ruled event kinds present), returned a bounded page (5 of 37), addressed a real cursor, classified a missing id as SESSION_MISSING, and left the artifact's sha256 unchanged.
The generation file's mtime, size and sha256 are byte-identical before and after two reads; two reads produced an identical sanitized projection.

Work AttemptId, HostJobId, Port InvocationId and DSH SessionId are four separate fields with four different producers, and no field is derived from another. The View ID is derived from (projectId, attemptId) and is explicitly not T0's asOf-bearing root id.

No durable Attempt→DSH Session producer exists. Every real product attempt reports SESSION_UNBOUND (or BOUND_LOCAL_ONLY from a host observation), and a caller-supplied id can never reach BOUND_VERIFIED. The missing producer, its authority and its failure semantics are recorded.
classifyBinding assigns BOUND_VERIFIED only when canonicalBindingPresent is true; a caller-supplied id plus an agreeing header yields BOUND_LOCAL_ONLY, and a header mismatch yields CONFLICT.
start() returned STARTED before completion; the Trajectory service then addressed the attempt by its canonical id from a separate caller with no host handle and no active main Agent Turn.
processLifecycle EXITED while canonical promotionState stayed NOT_PROMOTED and verificationState NOT_OBSERVED_BY_V0; the caveat is stated on every Preview.

A new delegation service reported the old handle as UNKNOWN and the Preview reported UNKNOWN_AFTER_RESTART, while the canonical attempt stayed COMPLETED and independently readable. No new host-job persistence was created.

Two independent projects started before either was awaited: distinct attempt ids, host jobs, port invocation ids, view ids and projection roots; neither Preview contains the other's events; both completed independently.

Supplying B's SessionId as A's claimed binding yielded SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE; a header naming a different session yielded CONFLICT; the same display label on two attempts produced two distinct identities.

All seven ruled event kinds are recognized and present in real logs; an unknown-but-valid kind is referenced by exact seq and never dropped or interpreted; a failed assistant/attempt keeps its failure status; a turn/end reports its reason and never asserts success.
A DSH event reference carries its own sessionId and local seq; DSH seq, Work project_sequence and host-observation sequence are never merged into one global sequence.

An inherited cut is marked from the source's own inheritedEventCount (seqs 0-2 inherited, seq 3 child-owned) and the parent is reported as a SESSION relation; the page carries no Work-delegation field.

A tool/call exposes the tool name and never its arguments; an assistant/message exposes position and no content or stream; the serialized page contains no 'arguments' key and none of the fixture secrets.

SESSION_MISSING is measured against a real absent id; CORRUPT_SESSION, FORMAT_UNSUPPORTED, BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE, IDENTITY_CONFLICT, EVENT_GAP and READ_CAPABILITY_ABSENT are exercised by the labelled fixture; an unsupported format is never an empty stream.
src/trajectory/projection.ts is unchanged and called through composeTrajectoryInputs; no second project-history engine was built.
The three relations with known-incomplete verifiers are quarantined as UNVERIFIED_RELATION and excluded from the selected set; every Preview states WORK_HISTORICAL_CUT_WITH_CURRENT_CROSS_OWNER_READS.
V0 selects an attempt by the canonical Work event's entity_id plus event type and project id, never by node.label.includes(attemptId).

One bounded, serializable model answers all ten ruled questions; two sanitized examples (a settled attempt and an incomplete/unbound attempt) are recorded with their exact source references and caveats.
There is no single COMPLETED boolean; process lifecycle, session lifecycle, canonical attempt state, verification, promotion and preview completeness are six separate fields.

The Preview cannot resume a session, schedule a worker, settle an attempt, approve a promotion, select capital or inject context: the module holds no owner and every input is a value. Its doesNotAuthorize list is asserted by test.
A structural field scan finds no permission, grant, token, budget, spend, capability or entitlement field anywhere in the model.

Two Preview builds left the work event count, chain digest, ProjectIR revision/digest, proof basis and reasoning bases unchanged; the Work owner's verifyFull still passes; the DSH artifact is byte-identical.
0 new canonical owners, 0 agent loops, 0 session stores, 0 schedulers, 0 automatic execution paths, 0 graph databases.
R3-L0C G0/G1/G1-B/IAR and T0 evidence namespaces are byte-identical; 0 changed, 0 removed.
architecture:check PASS — 0 violations, 9 accepted baseline exceptions observed (unchanged).
check-public-api PASS — 0 missing, 0 changed kind, 0 added.
The full suite is 318 files / 4516 tests with 15 failures — the identical archived-plan set as the T0 baseline; V0 adds 4 files and 56 tests, all passing.
No real model execution, no paid call, no provider contact, no PRIMARY enablement.

completionStateJustification: The real product's Work/Project Preview and independent asynchronous Attempt inspection work: one Handoff Preview combines canonical Work facts, host observations, the reused T0 project-evolution view and a real DSH session read, over real non-model Attempts, with two-attempt isolation proven and read-only safety measured. An authentic DSH Session BINDING is not established, because no Attempt→Session producer exists — the missing source is reported explicitly and a caller-supplied SessionId can never exceed BOUND_LOCAL_ONLY. The controlled DSH fixture retains its PASS_DSH_QUERY_PORT_FIXTURE class, and the real DSH read retains PASS_REAL_DSH_QUERY_NO_MODEL.

finalAcceptanceAnswer.question: Does the existing Palimpsest architecture, together with DeepSeek Harness's own Session history and the already-developed T0 Project Evolution projection, provide enough information to inspect one asynchronous Agent Attempt and prepare a safe, reviewable handoff—without building another Harness?
finalAcceptanceAnswer.whatWorks: Palimpsest can address an asynchronous Attempt by its canonical id after start() returns, read its real DSH session through DSH's own first-party persistence reader with no model and no activation, reuse the T0 project-evolution projection, and combine all of it into one bounded read-only Preview that keeps six statuses separate and refuses every wrong-source or self-declared claim.
finalAcceptanceAnswer.theGap: There is no durable Attempt→DSH Session binding producer, so the execution half is caller-addressed rather than authoritative for a real product attempt. That is the smallest necessary future integration, and its producer, authority and failure semantics are recorded.
